column1: Drivers use mmap followed by pgprot_* and remap_pfn_range or vm_insert_pfn
in order to export reserved memory to userspace. Currently
not tracked and hence not kept consistent with other mappings (/dev/mem
pci resource
column3: that may exist in the system.

column1: The following patchset adds x86 PAT attribute tracking and untracking for
pfnmap related APIs.
First three patches in the patchset are changing the generic mm code to fit
in this tracking. Last four patches are x86 specific to make things work
with x86 PAT code. The patchset aso introduces pgprot_writecombine interface
which gives writecombine mapping when enabled
pgprot_noncached otherwise.
This patch:
While working on x86 PAT
column2: we faced some hurdles with trackking

column1: remap_pfn_range() regions
column2: as we do not have any information to say

column1: whether that PFNMAP mapping is linear for the entire vma range or
it is smaller granularity regions within the vma.
A simple solution to this is to use vm_pgoff as an indicator for
linear mapping over the vma region. Currently
only sets vm_pgoff for COW mappings. Below patch changes the
logic and sets the vm_pgoff irrespective of COW. This will still not
be enough for the case where pfn is zero (vma region mapped to
physical address zero). But
pfnmap VMAs and say whether the mappng is for the entire vma region
or not.
